document_contents.title: Rodenstock explores private credit options for EUR810m TLB refi (9fin)
document_contents.key_findings: Sponsor Apax in early-stage talks with banks and private credit funds to refinance Rodenstock's EUR810m of TLB debt (EUR660m TLB due May-2028 + EUR150m TLB due Jul-2028), possibly via a hybrid syndicated/private-credit structure or an all-private-credit solution. Both loans priced at E+500bps (2021/2022) and were trading at 95.5 as of this article. Company generating ~EUR135m EBITDA at the time (sources). FY2023 actuals: EUR506m sales, EUR122m EBITDA before one-offs (Moody's). Apr-2024 Moody's affirmed B3 but moved outlook to negative, citing weaker-than-expected credit metrics over the next two years and the phase-out of the GrandVision contract as a key revenue driver of the slump. Apax bought Rodenstock from Compass Partners for EUR1.5bn in Mar-2021.

document_contents.title: Is Rodenstock seeing clearly? (9fin)
document_contents.key_findings: Origination piece for the 2021 EUR660m TLB + EUR120m RCF financing backing the Apax/Mubadala buyout (EV EUR1.275bn paid to Compass, marketed off EUR125m EBITDA, 10.2x EBITDA multiple at entry). Moody's-adjusted gross leverage 9.0x at 2021 (incl. pensions), expected to fall to ~8.0x in 2022; Fitch FFO gross leverage 9.5x in 2021, expected ~7.5x by 2023. RCF has a 9.5x springing net-leverage covenant, tested only if drawn >=40%, from 12 months post-close - company expected to have ample headroom. Facilities secured by share pledges, bank accounts and intercompany receivables, guaranteed by group companies representing >=80% of group EBITDA. Company has a long history of sponsor-driven financial stress: 2010-11 standstill agreement with lenders RBS/Societe Generale on EUR370m of debt under Bridgepoint ownership (with EUR190m unfunded German pension liabilities at the time), following earlier 2003 financial difficulties that triggered the original Permira sale. EUR75m equity injection from shareholders in Jun-2020 in response to pandemic-driven sales drop. Small scale versus peers (Essilor-Luxottica, Zeiss, Fielmann, Hoya) is repeatedly flagged as a structural risk to R&D and digitalisation investment capacity.

key_catalysts_notes_for_orchestrator: Maturity wall: EUR660m TLB due 21-May-2028 and EUR150m TLB due Jul-2028 - both inside the Phase 1 screen's 18-24 month window from 27-Sep-2026.

Refinancing status is the single biggest open question: a Mar-2025 9fin article shows the sponsor exploring private credit refinancing options for the full EUR810m TLB stack; a Jul-2026 Fitch B- IDR assignment plus a Jul-2026 Moody's rating withdrawal 'on issuer's request' both suggest something happened around that time (a completed refinancing that shifted primary rating coverage to Fitch is one plausible read, but this is not confirmed by any document found on 9fin - flag as a priority follow-up, likely resolved by a fresh 9fin news/document search closer to the tearsheet finalisation date, or by checking Moody's/Fitch press releases directly).

Rating trajectory is negative overall: B3 stable (pre-2024) -> B3 negative outlook (Apr-2024) -> Caa1 stable (Apr-2025, a downgrade) -> Moody's withdrawn (Jul-2026) alongside a fresh Fitch B- IDR (Jul-2026). Net effect: the company was downgraded into the Caa range at Moody's before its rating was pulled.

Operationally the business has been improving (FY2024 revenue EUR512.4m, adj. EBITDA EUR128.6m, +5.1% YoY) even as leverage-side credit metrics worsened - this combination (operational improvement, credit deterioration) is worth stating plainly in the situation overview rather than resolved either way, since it likely reflects continued high leverage/interest burden rather than a operating problem.
